question: Can one large vision-language-action policy become an out-of-the-box, steerable manipulation generalist by jointly conditioning on visual history, semantic subtasks, generated future images, quality and speed metadata, and mixed-quality multi-robot experience, without task-specific low-level post-training?

key_findings.claim: The proposed generalist is not merely a larger action policy: it turns several kinds of deployment-time context into optional controls over a single 5B-parameter VLA.
key_findings.evidence: The model combines a Gemma 3 4B VLM backbone, including a roughly 400M-parameter vision encoder, with an approximately 860M-parameter flow-matching action expert and a MEM-style history encoder. Inputs may include four current views, six one-second-spaced history frames per view, three generated subgoal views, task and subtask language, control mode, speed/quality/mistake metadata, and proprioception; the output is a 50-step action chunk.

anchors.section: VI-A-B Training data and model architecture, Figure 3

key_findings.claim: Steerability is learned through deliberately incomplete prompts and heterogeneous trajectory quality, so the same policy can be run with only a task or with progressively richer guidance.
key_findings.evidence: Generated goals appear on 25% of examples; when goals are present the semantic subtask is dropped 30% of the time. All metadata is dropped 15% of the time and each component another 5%, while the control-mode token is retained. History and rear-camera context are each dropped with probability 0.3. Speed is binned in 500-step units, quality is scored 1-5, and mistakes are coarsely annotated. The mixture includes expert demonstrations, failures, evaluation and π*0.6 rollouts, interventions, open robot data, egocentric human video, and web tasks; footnote 1 excludes autonomous data collected on the generalization-focused evaluation tasks from training.

anchors.section: V-C-E Episode metadata and prompt dropout
VI-A-B Training mixture and context dropout
IX-A metadata and evaluation-data ablation, Figure 7

key_findings.claim: The visual-goal mechanism is a separate 14B image world model that predicts multi-view future observations, not an emergent capability of the 5B VLA itself.
key_findings.evidence: A BAGEL 14B model is adapted to generate future camera views from the present observations and a subtask. Real future goals are sampled either from the end of a segment with probability 0.25 or uniformly zero to four seconds ahead with probability 0.75, and generated goals are mixed into VLA training. At runtime goals refresh on a subtask change or every four seconds. Appendix C says temporal segmentation and language-label quality materially control goal quality; Appendix D reports a 1.25-second world-model generation path on four H100 GPUs.

anchors.section: Appendix D, inference speed and optimization

key_findings.claim: Across the paper's in-house tasks, the strongest empirical story is increased throughput at similar success, especially on diverse long-horizon work, rather than a uniform success-rate gain.
key_findings.evidence: In Figure 6, π0.7 reaches roughly 1.48× the normalized throughput of the π*0.6 RL specialist on diverse hardest-item laundry and roughly 1.47× on box building, while success is about 73% versus 70% and 88% versus 88%, respectively. T-shirt laundry and espresso throughput are instead near 0.95× the specialist, with broadly comparable success. These are visual plot readings because exact values, counts, and uncertainty definitions are not printed.

key_findings.claim: Instruction following and referential grounding improve over π0.5 and π0.6, but complex relations remain substantially harder unless generated visual goals are supplied.
key_findings.evidence: Across 14 instruction scenarios in four unseen kitchens and two unseen bedrooms, Figure 9 reads approximately 87% kitchen and 73% bedroom instruction-following success for π0.7, versus about 54% for π0.6 and 25-28% for π0.5. In Figure 10, standard referential instructions are roughly 98% for π0.7, whereas complex relations are only about 38%; goal conditioning raises the complex case to about 64% while leaving the standard case near 96%. Values are approximate visual readings, and trial counts and the error-bar definition are not printed beside the bars.

key_findings.claim: The model shows meaningful zero-shot transfer to held-out robot-task pairs, but the breadth is constrained to parallel-jaw manipulators and performance remains below coached variants or the human reference on the hardest tasks.
key_findings.evidence: Figure 12 visually reports shirt bagging near 94% for π0.7 versus roughly 67% for π0.6 and 57% for π0.5. On held-out towel and shirt folding, π0.7 is about 60% and 68%; generated-goal conditioning raises these to roughly 77% and 86%. Figure 13 qualitatively shows a single-arm bag-insertion strategy and vertical cloth grasps on the UR5e that differ from source-robot demonstrations. The human progress reference is 90.9%. The platforms vary in geometry but all use parallel-jaw grippers.

key_findings.claim: On the headline dexterous comparison, π0.7 nearly matches a small group of highly experienced teleoperators, but the published percentage is arithmetically under-specified.
key_findings.evidence: Ten teleoperators from the top 2% by experience, averaging about 375 total hours, receive no practice and perform three trials each; the paper reports 90.9% mean progress and 80.6% success for humans, versus 85.6% progress and 80.0% success for π0.7. With 30 equally weighted binary human trials, success can change only in 3.33-point increments, so 80.6% cannot be the raw pooled fraction. No alternate weighting, policy trial count, interval, or significance test is stated.

key_findings.claim: Long-horizon tasks that fail under a direct instruction can be bootstrapped from up to five minutes of human coaching, after which a separate language policy supplies subtasks or generated goals.
key_findings.evidence: The paper explicitly says direct prompting does not solve the unseen long-horizon tasks. A human remotely provides corrective guidance, and that trace trains a high-level language policy. Figure 15 reads loading an air fryer at about 97-98% progress with language or goal-conditioned coaching versus roughly 13% for π0.5 and 24% for π0.6; for toasting a bagel, goal-conditioned coaching is about 80% versus roughly 48% with language-only coaching and 29-48% for direct prior models.

anchors.section: IX-D coaching protocol and no action-level target-task data

key_findings.claim: The slogan 'without task-specific post-training' is accurate for the low-level VLA but does not describe the entire coached autonomy stack.
key_findings.evidence: The low-level π0.7 weights are reused across evaluated tasks, including unseen task/robot combinations. However, the long-horizon demonstrations train a task-facing high-level language policy from coaching traces and may invoke the separate goal-image generator. Thus the paper demonstrates no task-specific low-level VLA adaptation, not an entirely task-training-free system.

key_findings.claim: Ablations support quality metadata and retaining the highest-diversity data, while generated goals on short tasks and end-effector control in prior models do not show a uniform advantage.
key_findings.evidence: Figure 18's raw laundry throughput rises from about 13 successes/hour at the top 30% of data to about 23 at 100% when metadata is present, while the no-metadata curve falls from about 12 at 80% to about 9 at 100%. Removing the highest-diversity 20% depresses scoop/spin/wipe success to roughly 32%/8%/6%, versus about 51%/36%/47% after removing a random 20%. Figure 17 is mixed—generated goals improve three short tasks but reduce scoop-rice success—and Appendix Figure 20 finds no consistent end-effector advantage for π0.5/π0.6 baseline policies, not for π0.7 itself.

key_findings.claim: The generalization claims are deliberately qualified by the authors: 'unseen' cannot be made cleanly disjoint from a large and heterogeneous pretraining mixture.
key_findings.evidence: The discussion states that separating truly seen from unseen behavior is difficult because skills can occur incidentally, appear in external human data, or be remixed from related tasks. The authors summarize observed performance as often above 90% on seen tasks but around 60-80% on unseen tasks and unseen robot-task combinations, which is evidence of useful transfer rather than proof of de novo skill acquisition.

key_findings.claim: The appendix reveals a material systems cost behind richer context, especially visual goals, that the main capability plots do not price into throughput.
key_findings.evidence: Minimal VLA inference is reported at 38 ms on one H100, while the largest MEM-plus-goal configuration reaches 127 ms. The BAGEL world model uses four H100s with tensor parallelism, 8-bit matrix multiplications, SageAttention, and 25 denoising steps for a 1.25-second generation. The action policy uses five denoising steps and executes only 15 or 25 of 50 predicted actions; training injects zero to 12 action steps of delay, at most 240 ms at 50 Hz.

key_findings.claim: The evaluation is broad but not independently reproducible from the paper: the benchmarks, training corpus scale, model weights, raw trajectories, and per-condition denominators are not supplied.
key_findings.evidence: Pages 24-25 provide detailed scoring rubrics for laundry, box assembly, dexterous packing, and folding, but many main figures omit exact bar values, trial counts, error-bar definitions, and statistical tests. The paper compares mostly against earlier in-house π models and in-house specialists on proprietary robots and tasks; it does not run a same-task external generalist baseline.

Appendix G task definitions and scoring

method.core_idea: Train one flow-matching VLA on a large multi-robot mixture while exposing optional context that says what to do, what success should look like, how quickly and carefully to act, and whether the trajectory is making a mistake; at deployment, add only the context needed for the task.
method.mechanism: Current multi-camera images, MEM-style image history, text tokens, optional BAGEL-generated future views, metadata, and proprioception are embedded into a Gemma 3-based backbone and an action expert. The action expert denoises continuous action chunks by flow matching. Prompt dropout forces compatibility with sparse and rich interfaces. Mixed expert, suboptimal, evaluation, and specialist-rollout data associates quality and strategy tokens with behavior. At runtime the controller requests quality 5, no mistake, a 15th-percentile speed, refreshes goals every four seconds or on subtask change, performs five denoising steps, and executes a prefix of each 50-step chunk. A high-level language model and optional goal generator can convert coaching-derived task plans into subtask and image context.
assumptions: Trajectory-level quality, speed, and mistake labels are sufficiently consistent that conditioning separates desirable behavior from merely imitating the mixture average.
The distribution of suboptimal and autonomous rollouts covers useful corrections rather than teaching unrecoverable or unsafe behavior.
A future image generated from current views and a subtask is geometrically and semantically accurate enough to guide action across camera viewpoints.
Prompt dropout makes missing context a supported deployment mode instead of an out-of-distribution input.
Skills learned across the proprietary robot mixture compose into genuinely new task/embodiment combinations despite incomplete train-test disjointness.
Delay randomization up to 240 ms and partial-chunk execution cover the relevant closed-loop latency distribution.
Progress rubrics and success criteria on pages 24-25 are sufficiently comparable across policies and human operators to support aggregate comparisons.
Parallel-jaw manipulation is an adequate test bed for the claimed cross-embodiment generality.

techniques.role: Conditions one VLA on task language, semantic subtasks, generated multi-view goals, robot/control identity, and behavioral metadata.
Labels mixed-quality demonstrations and policy rollouts by speed, quality, and mistakes so deployment can request the desirable tail.
Compresses up to six prior frames per camera at one-second spacing to expose temporally distant state without a full video-token sequence.
Generates up to three future camera observations from present views and subtask language for goal-conditioned manipulation.
Randomly removes history, cameras, goals, subtasks, and metadata during training so the policy supports a hierarchy of deployment interfaces.
Uses a separate action expert and five-step denoising to predict 50 continuous actions, of which 15 or 25 are executed before replanning.
Shifts target actions by zero to 12 steps during training to make the policy robust to up to 240 ms of control delay at 50 Hz.
Collects corrective high-level traces for tasks that direct prompting cannot solve, then trains a language planner rather than the low-level VLA.
Combines conditional and unconditional action predictions with task-dependent guidance strengths from 1.3 to 2.2.

evaluations.result: π0.7 is approximately 0.95×/1.48×/0.95×/1.47× specialist throughput on T-shirt laundry/diverse hardest-item laundry/espresso/box building, with success near 94%/73%/92%/88%
evaluations.baseline: π*0.6 RL specialist fixed at 1.0 throughput, with success near 91%/70%/95%/88%; values are plot readings and exact denominators are absent

evaluations.result: Full π0.7 is 1.0 throughput on every task; no-metadata is roughly 0.76/0.52/0.64/0.25 and no-evaluation-data roughly 0.66/0.59/0.62/0.57 on T-shirt laundry/diverse laundry/espresso/box

limitations: Author-stated: because training is extremely heterogeneous, it is difficult to classify a task or skill as truly unseen; related behavior may occur incidentally or be assembled from familiar parts.
Author-stated: seen tasks often exceed 90%, whereas unseen tasks and unseen robot-task combinations remain roughly in the 60-80% range.
Author-stated: generated-goal quality depends strongly on accurate temporal segmentation and semantic labels, as Appendix C illustrates.

Reviewer-identified: the model, data, training scale, benchmark assets, and raw trajectories are not released or enumerated in the paper, preventing independent replication and contamination analysis.

Reviewer-identified: many plots omit exact numeric labels, trial denominators, error-bar definitions, and hypothesis tests; the 80.6% human success number is incompatible with an unweighted pool of 30 binary trials.
Reviewer-identified: all evaluated hardware uses parallel-jaw grippers, so cross-embodiment evidence does not cover hands, suction, locomotion, or radically different action spaces.
Reviewer-identified: external human video may contain objects and appliance interactions similar to the held-out tasks, weakening a strict zero-shot interpretation.
Reviewer-identified: the human study samples ten elite operators for three trials each and does not report matched policy denominators or confidence intervals.
Reviewer-identified: most baselines are earlier in-house π variants or in-house specialists; there is no same-task head-to-head against Gemini Robotics, LAP, or another external generalist.
Reviewer-identified: the visual-goal path is expensive—14B parameters, four H100s, and 1.25 seconds—and its latency is not charged in the manipulation-throughput plots.
Reviewer-identified: Appendix Figure 20 compares joint and end-effector control only for π0.5 and π0.6; it cannot establish control-space invariance for π0.7.
Reviewer-identified: no task-specific post-training applies to the low-level VLA, while coached long-horizon autonomy still trains a high-level policy on task-specific traces.
failure_modes: A generated future image can hallucinate an impossible object pose, wrong camera geometry, or a state inconsistent across views, pulling the action policy toward an unrecoverable target.
Poor temporal segmentation or vague subtask labels can train the world model on mismatched present/future pairs and degrade goal guidance.
Requesting high quality and no mistake from a sparsely labeled mixture may extrapolate beyond combinations actually demonstrated rather than reliably select expert behavior.
History compression can preserve stale observations or omit the brief event needed to disambiguate whether an object was grasped, dropped, or moved off camera.
A high-level coaching policy can issue a plausible but physically infeasible subtask, and the low-level VLA has no demonstrated formal mechanism for rejecting it.
Executing 15 or 25 actions open loop can amplify contact errors before the next observation, especially when deployment latency exceeds the zero-to-240-ms training randomization.
Direct language prompting can fail entirely on unseen long-horizon tasks even when the constituent low-level skills exist; the demonstrated remedy requires new coaching traces.

Generated goals add little on some short tasks, while end-effector control shows no clear overall improvement, so extra context or a seemingly more invariant action space can add complexity without benefit.
Training on evaluation and specialist rollouts can import their systematic errors; metadata is only useful if it distinguishes those errors accurately.
A task categorized as zero-shot can in fact overlap unreported pretraining, making apparent emergence a retrieval or recombination effect.
reusable_insights: Represent policy improvement as conditional behavior selection: keep imperfect rollouts, but label their speed, quality, and mistakes so a single policy can learn both what happens and which mode to request.
Use independent dropout for each steering channel so a controller remains usable with task language alone and improves gracefully as history, plans, or goals become available.
Separate high-level coaching from low-level motor adaptation when a general motor policy already contains the necessary primitives; this localizes task-specific data collection to a cheaper layer.
Generated observations can be a shared interface between a semantic planner and a continuous controller, provided temporal alignment and camera consistency are audited.
Evaluate generalists on throughput as well as binary success: faster recovery and better pacing may matter even when endpoint success saturates.

Use matched removal controls to value diversity: removing the highest-diversity 20% versus a random 20% isolates which data contribute to compositional transfer without changing retained dataset size.
Publish rubric-level scoring definitions for partial progress, but also publish the raw denominators and uncertainty needed to audit aggregate claims.
Latency randomization should be stated in physical time and evaluated against the complete planner-plus-world-model system, not only the action network.
open_questions: How much of π0.7's improvement comes from model architecture, more diverse data, quality metadata, specialist-rollout distillation, or the particular prompt-dropout schedule under a factorial comparison?
Can a visual-goal model expose calibrated uncertainty or cross-view consistency checks before its images influence physical actions?
Would the reported zero-shot transfer survive a benchmark with auditable train-test provenance and tasks designed after data collection?
How does π0.7 compare with external generalist VLAs on shared public robots and tasks under matched compute and demonstrations?
What are the exact per-task trial counts, confidence intervals, and aggregation rule behind the 80.6% human success result?
Can coaching be made online and continual without catastrophic interference in the high-level policy or accumulating unsafe subtask conventions?
Does quality conditioning reliably reject bad behavior under distribution shift, or can it merely reproduce correlations between metadata and familiar environments?
Can the four-H100 visual-goal path be distilled or cached enough to improve wall-clock task throughput, not only action-level progress?
Does the approach transfer to dexterous hands, suction, tool-changing, or mobile manipulation with substantially different action representations?
What safety behavior occurs when task language, generated images, metadata, and observed history disagree?

competitive_landscape.title: π0: A Vision-Language-Action Flow Model for General Robot Control
competitive_landscape.difference: π0 establishes the flow-matching VLA/action-expert architecture and heterogeneous multi-robot control. π0.7 builds on that base with MEM history, behavior metadata, generated visual subgoals, prompt dropout, and distillation of suboptimal/evaluation/specialist rollouts rather than introducing the base architecture.

competitive_landscape.title: π0.5: a Vision-Language-Action Model with Open-World Generalization
competitive_landscape.difference: π0.5 already co-trains heterogeneous robot data, web data, high-level semantic prediction, and hybrid multimodal examples for unseen-home generalization. π0.7's narrower increment is explicit steering by quality/strategy metadata, MEM history, multi-view future-image prompts, and mixed-quality policy-rollout distillation.

competitive_landscape.title: Hi Robot: Open-Ended Instruction Following with Hierarchical Vision-Language-Action Models
competitive_landscape.difference: Hi Robot already composes a high-level VLM with a low-level VLA for open-ended instructions, feedback, and new environments. π0.7 puts more optional steering context into one low-level generalist and uses a coaching-trained high-level policy for tasks that still require hierarchy.

competitive_landscape.title: Zero-Shot Robotic Manipulation with Pretrained Image-Editing Diffusion Models
competitive_landscape.difference: SuSIE already uses a pretrained image-editing diffusion model as a visual-subgoal planner paired with a goal-conditioned robot policy. π0.7 explicitly follows this visual-planning line but generates multi-camera futures with BAGEL and makes goals one optional channel alongside memory and metadata in a much larger VLA.

competitive_landscape.title: MEM: Multi-Scale Embodied Memory for Vision Language Action Models
competitive_landscape.difference: MEM supplies the multi-scale visual-history mechanism used by π0.7. The present paper integrates it with behavior metadata, generated goals, mixed-quality data, and broader out-of-box evaluations rather than claiming memory itself as new.

competitive_landscape.title: π*0.6: a VLA That Learns From Experience
competitive_landscape.difference: π*0.6 uses RECAP-style task-specific experience, interventions, and advantage conditioning to make specialist policies. π0.7 distills such specialist and evaluation rollouts, together with quality metadata, into one reusable generalist rather than performing task-specific low-level RL at deployment.

competitive_landscape.title: Gemini Robotics: Bringing AI into the Physical World
competitive_landscape.difference: Gemini Robotics already reports broad instruction following, dexterity, new-environment generalization, and adaptation to new embodiments. π0.7's differentiator is context-conditioned selection from mixed-quality data and zero-shot low-level reuse, while Gemini Robotics also studies embodiment adaptation; the present paper does not establish superiority on a shared benchmark.

competitive_landscape.title: LAP: Language-Action Pre-Training Enables Zero-shot Cross-Embodiment Transfer
competitive_landscape.difference: LAP already demonstrates zero-shot transfer to held-out embodiments by pretraining natural-language action representations. π0.7 instead retains continuous flow-matched robot actions and uses diverse demonstrations, metadata, history, and image goals; its cross-embodiment results therefore are not the first zero-shot VLA evidence, but a different transfer route.

competitive_landscape.title: ForeAct: Steering Your VLA with Efficient Visual Foresight Planning
competitive_landscape.difference: ForeAct already steers an existing VLA with generated future observations and textual subtasks, reporting 0.33-second 640×480 generation on one H100 and 87.4% success over 11 real tasks. π0.7 folds multi-view goals into training as one optional context channel alongside metadata and memory, but its 1.25-second four-H100 goal path is not the first or most compute-efficient visual-foresight interface.

competitive_landscape.title: Data Analogies Enable Efficient Cross-Embodiment Transfer
competitive_landscape.difference: Data Analogies controls viewpoint, morphology, scene, and trajectory alignment and reports that paired cross-embodiment demonstrations improve real-world transfer by 22.5 percentage points over larger unpaired mixtures. π0.7 instead relies on broad heterogeneous pretraining and optional visual goals; its results therefore do not isolate whether raw diversity or aligned analogies cause the transfer.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: π0.7 is presented as a new generation of steerable robotic foundation model that acquires emergent dexterity, instruction following, cross-embodiment transfer, and rapid coaching while working out of the box without task-specific low-level post-training.
novelty_assessment.evidence: One 5B flow VLA is evaluated over seen, unseen-environment, compositional-instruction, held-out robot-task, dexterous, and coached long-horizon regimes. It accepts optional memory, metadata, language, and BAGEL-generated goals; it reaches 85.6% dexterous progress versus 90.9% for elite humans, roughly 60-80% on several unseen regimes, and substantially improves coached long-horizon progress. Ablations support metadata and task diversity.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The credible novelty is the integration and scale of steerability: a π0-family flow VLA learns optional behavior metadata, temporal memory, generated multi-view goals, and distilled mixed-quality experience in one out-of-box low-level policy. Each major ingredient has a close predecessor—π0/π0.5 for the VLA and open-world co-training, MEM for history, SuSIE and ForeAct for visual subgoals, Hi Robot for hierarchy, π*0.6 for experience-conditioned improvement, and LAP/Data Analogies for cross-embodiment transfer—so the novelty should not be phrased as the first generalist, first zero-shot cross-embodiment VLA, first visual-goal robot policy, or a wholly task-training-free system. The breadth is impressive, but proprietary data, unmatched external baselines, ambiguous denominators, and incomplete train-test provenance keep the emergence claim suggestive rather than causally isolated.
